q: Which of these tasks can a drone equipped with a sensor currently help with?
explain: A drone equipped with a sensor can quickly cover a field to detect pest outbreaks, while harvesting, hand-weeding, and detasseling still require manual labor or specialized equipment.

q: In a SWOT analysis of drones in agriculture, limited battery life restricting mission length is an example of a:
explain: Battery life is an internal limitation of the technology itself, which makes it a weakness rather than an external opportunity or threat.

q: Why does using drones for scouting help decrease inter-rater variability?
options: Drones are cheaper than hiring scouts
Sensor data is collected consistently, rather than depending on individual human judgment
Drones do not require any training to operate
explain: When different people scout a field by eye, their assessments can vary. A sensor collects data the same way every time, reducing that variability between different raters.

q: AI-assisted image analysis automating pest and stress detection is best described as which part of a SWOT analysis?
explain: This is a developing capability that could expand what drones are able to do in the future, which makes it an opportunity rather than a current strength.

q: After a hailstorm damages a field, what is one way a drone could help an agronomist make a harvest decision?
options: By replacing the need for crop insurance
By mapping the extent and severity of leaf damage across the field
explain: A drone can quickly map defoliation patterns and damage severity across an entire field, giving the agronomist the information needed to decide whether to replant, treat, or proceed to harvest.

q: Why are drones useful for measuring large plant breeding panels like the IMDP?
options: They can capture consistent data across every plot quickly, instead of walking each plot by hand
They eliminate the need for any data analysis
They can physically cross plants together
They replace the need for a breeding program entirely
explain: Walking every plot by hand is slow and can introduce inconsistency between measurements. A drone can fly the same panel in minutes, capturing consistent data across all plots in a single pass.

q: Which of these remains a task that drones cannot yet help with?
explain: Harvesting crops still requires specialized heavy equipment that drones are not currently capable of replacing.
